name: Pakistan
headline: Pakistan: +3.2% growth in 2025, 4.5% inflation, debt 73% of GDP
sections: Pakistan is a $408 billion economy (2025), the world's 42nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.2% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $6,573 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 13.0% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 4.5% in 2025, above typical targets, down from 12.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 7.1% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 9.6% (2025).
Gross government debt is 73% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 81% in 2020. The general government balance is −5.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +0.5% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 27% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.5% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 57% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 67.8 years (2024). Population: 240.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
